title: ChatGPT: A means to enable student critical thinking in large classes
venue: Proceedings of the Fifth PHELC Symposium
extended_summary:
This paper is a short conference proceedings contribution about the potential use of ChatGPT in higher education large-class teaching. It addresses the problem of how educators might use generative AI to support critical thinking and student engagement in large classes, rather than reporting a controlled evaluation of learning outcomes. The paper appears in a higher-education teaching symposium and is framed around pedagogical possibilities rather than causal impact testing.

The intervention discussed is ChatGPT as a teaching and learning aid. However, in the text provided here, there is no reported experiment, no treatment-versus-control comparison, no random assignment, and no extractable outcome statistics on motivation or writing performance. There is also no evidence in the provided text of a secondary or high-school writing study, no 25-plus-25 student design, and no 12-week randomized trial. Instead, the surrounding proceedings clearly situate the contribution in higher education, with Willie Golden of the University of Galway presenting a short paper on ChatGPT in large classes.

The population context is therefore undergraduate higher education, likely at a single university context in Ireland, though participant-level details are not reported in the provided text. No sample size, measures, or implementation details are given. Because no empirical results are included here, the paper cannot support any quantitative inference about ChatGPT effects on student motivation or writing quality.

For the verification task described, this item is not the alleged 2026 motivation randomized controlled trial with implausible effect size around d≈19. Based on the provided text, it should not be included in a quantitative synthesis of ChatGPT-based writing feedback in high school because it is not a high-school study, not a writing-feedback trial, and not an RCT with extractable statistics.
